gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 600 W kit ($798) refills its 1,024 Wh battery in about 1.7 h of full sun from its own panel (1,024 Wh ÷ 600 W). That is about 2.3 h at runtimemath's 75% derate. This beats every kit the rival pages rank, including runtimemath's fastest at 2.7 h, Dealectric's at 2.9 h and Trek4Tech's at 5.4 h.
standout_why: Pages read: trek4tech.com (cited), runtimemath.com, solarpanelx.com and our own dealectric.com page. theoutageplan.com (cited) would not load because of an SSL certificate error, so it was not checked. Trek4Tech's fastest kit is the River 2 Pro + 220 W at 5.4 h (Wh ÷ 0.65 × panel W), and it gives no prices. Runtimemath's fastest is the R1500 + SP039 at 2.7 sun hours, built from separately bought parts at $938. SolarPanelX's fastest is the DELTA 3 + 220 W, 'within 6 hrs'. Our page's fastest is the AC180 + 2×200 W at 2.9 h for $1,232. None of these pages lists the P1800 + 600 W bundle or compares the P1800 400 W and 600 W kits on hours to full.
decides: This changes the pick. ChatGPT chose the P1800 + 400 W ($698, 1,024 ÷ 400 = 2.56 h). The same station with the 600 W panel costs $100 more and refills in 1,024 ÷ 600 = 1.71 h, a third less sun time. The station's 650 W solar input can take the whole panel at its rating. For the question 'recharges fastest from its own panels', the P1800 + 600 W leads every kit found with a sourced price. Possible limit: the SP039 is a 44 V panel, so it draws about 13.6 A (600 ÷ 44). If the P1800 has a 13 A limit like the R1500 (not confirmed), it would charge at about 572 W, giving 1,024 ÷ 572 = 1.79 h. That is still the fastest.
